data.budget: read-only, ~1 h, no full test suite
data.claim: A first-time operator reaches a merged task in about 12 commands at ~1.2 s each idle, but falls off at: 3 entry points (init/adopt/onboard), a 10-gate pipeline for a trivial task, no tour/next-steps/why/explain/completion commands, a 470 KB README as the only getting-started, 1-35 s CLI latency on the 116 MB log, and typo hints buried after an 80-command dump.
data.falsifier: A fresh user completes init to complete in under 5 commands without reading the README, or CLI cheap commands on the big project stay under 1 s on an idle machine.
data.mechanism: Defaults and help were built for the enforced contract, not for first success; discovery commands and a fast path are absent; cost scales with the log fold, not the question asked.
data.probe: scratch project: ddflow init/phase add/task add/next/claim/gate status/merge/complete/clam/tour/explain/why; timings on both projects at load avg 64; transcript and event-log counts (python3 -I); WebFetch clig.dev and Anthropic writing-tools-for-agents
data.probe_output: version 1.1 s; scratch cheap cmds 1.0-1.7 s; big project brief 35 s, status 24.6 s, next 7.2 s, show 6.4 s, approvals pending 7.5 s (load 64); session start 9539 tokens (tools/list 8592); merge landed with zero gates; tour/next-steps/explain/why/completion: invalid choice; 132275 events, 39427 lease.renewed
data.question: Where does a new operator or agent lose time or calls in ddflow 0.2.10, and what do comparable tools do better?
